event_name: Rattlesnake Flats Road burnover (hand crew strike team STG1 during firing preparation)
agency_report_type: CAL FIRE Green Sheet 18-CA-BTU-016737 (Informational Summary Report)
people_involved: Two CAL FIRE hand crews (CRW1, CRW2) with two Fire Captains; 3 injured (1 Fire Captain, 2 inmate firefighters)
outcome: 3 serious burn injuries, transported to burn center; no fatalities; no fire shelter deployment reported
key_timing: Fire start 06:29 (report 06:33). STG1 assigned 12:45; scouting 13:30; briefing 13:55; firing plan 14:15, fire estimated 1/4 mile north of Rattlesnake Flats Rd backing south. ~14:45 sudden wind shift, ~25 mph, 10 to 15 ft flames, fire crossed road cutting egress west then east; ~20 ft of defensive firing completed before front overtook CRW1 egress. ~15:00 STLG1 returned and found injured; ALS transport ~15:30. First emergency traffic call went unanswered due to radio congestion. NIST TN 2135 Table 33/34 lists this burnover at 15:15, duration 15 min (shortest of 19), road width 3 m, vegetation setback 0 m, 300 m of road affected.
weather_at_event: Burnover weather: 61 F, RH 12%, wind 10 mph NE gusting 28 mph, good visibility. Jarbo Gap RAWS: NE winds 25 to 30 mph sustained, gusts 45 to 50 mph overnight; RH about 10% by Thursday afternoon.
fire_behavior: Fuel Model 1 (moderately grazed grass), slope 5%, SW aspect, elevation 500 ft. Wind-driven run in flashy fuels after sudden wind shift; incident-wide ROS about 100 ch/h, spotting to 1 mile.
escape_route_safety_zone_notes: Escape routes along road cut off in both directions by fire crossing; barbed-wire fences on both sides of road obstructed escape (one firefighter collided with fence, one snagged by tool on web gear). Crew used defensive firing and refuge in the burn and at crew transports.
relevance_to_UQ: Direct firefighter case where T_fire_arrival collapsed within minutes of a wind shift and T_notify failed (emergency traffic unanswered), giving a calibration point for negative margin under wind-shift uncertainty.

event_name: Chestnut Circle propane tank BLEVE, engine crew burn injuries (Magalia)
agency_report_type: CAL FIRE Green Sheet 18-CA-BTU-016737 and Blue Sheet (preliminary)
people_involved: Engine E1 crew of 3 (1 Fire Captain, 2 Fire Fighter I); 2 injured
outcome: 2 burn injuries (Fire Captain and Fire Fighter I), treated at local hospital; not an entrapment by NWCG definition (explosion hazard)
key_timing: E1 told of structure protection need on Ponderosa Way ~04:50 Nov 9 (14 h after Rattlesnake Flats burnover); ~05:00 observed burning structures and a 5 ft x 5 ft spot fire on Chestnut Circle. Green Sheet gives ~05:00; Blue Sheet gives ~06:00 (discrepancy between the two CAL FIRE documents). NIST TN 2135 lists Chestnut Cir burnover at 06:00 Nov 9.
weather_at_event: 49 F, RH 18%, wind 30 mph NE gusting 46 mph, low visibility
fire_behavior: Fuel Model 10 mixed conifer supplemented by structures, outbuildings and vehicles; partially filled 250 gallon residential propane tank under direct flame impingement. Slope 5 to 10%, W aspect, elevation 2,340 ft.
escape_route_safety_zone_notes: Hazard was a WUI explosion rather than fire front arrival; illustrates non-vegetation hazards not captured by T_fire_arrival.
relevance_to_UQ: Shows WUI structure-protection hazards (BLEVE) that sit outside a fire-arrival margin model and should be treated as a separate hazard term.

event_name: NIST catalogue of 19 documented burnover locations (first 24 h), including first responder shelter use at Hoffman Rd and Pearson Rd
agency_report_type: NIST Technical Note 2135, Section 9.3 and Tables 33 to 34
people_involved: Civilians and first responders (counts per event not tabulated as totals); Rattlesnake Flats was the only one of the 19 involving hand crews
outcome: Civilian fatalities and injuries, first responder injuries, vehicle damage; fire shelters deployed in 2 cases (Hoffman Rd: shelter used to shield a first responder and civilians during rescue; Pearson Rd: shelter deployed inside fire engine against window, engine exterior damaged)
key_timing: First burnovers ~07:50 Nov 8 (Hoffman Rd, 40 min duration; Concow Rd); Chapman Ln and upper Skyway 08:30 (Skyway 360 min); Pentz Rd 08:45 (150 min); Pearson Rd 09:15 (60 min); Bille Rd 09:25 (140 min); Rattlesnake Flats 15:15 (15 min); last two ~07:15 Nov 9 (Ponderosa Way, Concow Fire Station 37). Most burnovers lasted 1 to 2 h; affected road length 150 m to 3000 m; road widths 3 m to 23 m; vegetation setback 0 m to 10 m.
weather_at_event: Strong NE downslope wind event; local winds estimated 22 to 27 m/s on Rim Rd at 07:20 Nov 8, while some spot fires in Paradise burned under near calm conditions
fire_behavior: Wind-driven ember-dominated spread; 11 Category 1 (highest risk) and 7 Category 2 burnovers; 6 Category 1 events led to Temporary Refuge Areas
escape_route_safety_zone_notes: Burnovers blocked pre-planned evacuation routes; gridlock on Pearson Rd and Skyway increased residence time and exposure; first responders drove through conditions judged unsafe for civilians; TRAs used as de facto safety zones.
relevance_to_UQ: Provides timed, located burnover durations and road geometry that can serve as validation targets for T_fire_arrival and egress-route blockage in the margin model.

relevance_to_UQ: Largest single-fire burnover catalogue for a benchmark fire; its 23-event list is the natural event set for validating the margin on Camp.

event_name: Carr Fire burnover fatalities and multiple entrapments (Dozer 1, Marin County engine ENG1, Redding FPI1, Dozers 2 to 4, PREV1, SUP1) incl. fire tornado
agency_report_type: CAL FIRE Green Sheet 18-CA-SHU-007808 and Blue Sheet (preliminary); NWCG Safety Gram 2018
people_involved: NWCG Safety Gram 2018 lists 8 involved (3 dozers, 1 engine crew, 2 overhead at separate locations) in the burn injury entry and 7 involved with 2 fatalities in the fatality entry; Green Sheet: 2 fatalities, Dozer 4 operator burned, 3 engine firefighters minor burns
outcome: 2 fatalities (dozer operator: thermal injuries, fire shelter not effectively used; Redding Fire Prevention Inspector: traumatic injuries in fire tornado); Dozer 4 operator burns to hands, neck and back and deployed shelter; ENG1 3 firefighters minor burns (1 referred to UC Davis Burn Center)
key_timing: ~17:30 fire transitions from fuel-dominated to wind-driven; all events within ~1 h 50 min over a 3 mile expanse. Dozer 1: 17:30 drove east from water treatment plant, 17:40 passing plant, photo 17:44, radio between 17:46 and 17:50 that operator was on a bench trying to make a safety zone, 17:50 helicopter drops, 18:08 helicopter forced to land (temperature warning), 18:10 to 18:13 burnover reported to DIVS and Branch. ENG1: 18:45 strike team arrives, 19:05 increased heat and smoke, crew retreats to engine/outbuilding, 19:27 injury reported. Fire tornado sequence: 18:38 ATGS advises Branch III to evacuate, 18:43 Branch IV warns fire will cross, 19:23 front crests hill, 19:35 FPI1 responds, 19:39 driving south on Buenaventura Blvd, 19:40 mayday. Blue Sheet gives ~18:40 for the dramatic increase in fire behavior (differs from Green Sheet 17:30).
weather_at_event: Mule Mountain RAWS (~4 mi away, 2,044 ft): 111 F at 18:00 July 26, RH single digits, gusts to 21 mph; 54 F coast to valley temperature difference drove strong thermal/marine push
fire_behavior: Spread observed at 2.5 mph; plume to ~40,000 ft; fire tornado ~1000 ft diameter at base, winds 136 to 165 mph (EF-3), peak gas temperatures likely over 2,700 F; all live vegetation under 1 inch consumed
escape_route_safety_zone_notes: Dozer operator attempted to build a safety zone on a bench under deteriorating conditions; others used road cut banks and a park as temporary refuge; ATGS evacuation advisory preceded the FPI1 burnover by about 60 minutes.
relevance_to_UQ: Best-timed benchmark case: the 18:38 warning to 19:40 mayday interval and 17:44 to 17:50 dozer sequence give direct values for T_notify and the realized margin under extreme plume-driven behavior.

event_name: West Altadena evacuation alert timing (civilian warning, not firefighter entrapment)
agency_report_type: LA County Investigation Report of the Eaton Fire Evacuation Alerts (May 2026, Citygate) and McChrystal Group AAR (Sept 2025)
people_involved: Civilian population west of Lake Ave, Altadena (no counts extracted)
outcome: Evacuation orders for 13 zones west of Lake Ave issued 03:25; fire front reached 1 block west of Lake Ave by 05:13
key_timing: 01:00 to 02:00: ~30 separate structure fires, a new request about every 2 minutes; 02:00 to 02:18 radio reports of fire entering northern Altadena; 02:18 IC begins west-side evacuation zone process; ~03:00 OEM rep relays zones to EOC; 03:25 orders for 13 zones issued; 03:53 front still ~2 blocks east of Lake Ave (FireGuard); 05:13 front crosses 1 block west (FireGuard); conflagration well underway by 06:00. Unified Command had no aerial fire spread intelligence 01:00 to 02:00 (aircraft grounded by wind from 18:45 Jan 7 per county timeline).
weather_at_event: Santa Ana wind event; county timeline notes gusts to 85 mph at 19:00 Jan 7 and 77 mph Jan 8
fire_behavior: Two-front fire; western front driven out of Eaton, Rubio and Echo canyons in 4 pushes into Altadena, then building-to-building conflagration
escape_route_safety_zone_notes: Decision chain IC to OEM field rep to EOC to alert system took about 67 minutes (02:18 to 03:25).
relevance_to_UQ: Gives a measured T_detect to T_notify pipeline (about 67 min from IC decision to issued order, and roughly 108 min of lead before front crossing) for the notification term of the margin.

event_name: Engine 6162 (Novato FPD) crew entrapment, fatality and burn injuries, 920 Orchard Lane, Wynola
agency_report_type: CDF Green Sheet (CACNF-003056 / CACSR-000132); CDF Review Report; Novato FPD Incident Recovery Report (May 26, 2004); NIOSH fatality report; NWCG Safety Gram 2003
people_involved: 4 (Engine 6162 crew: Captain, 2 Engineers, Fire Fighter/Paramedic) of Strike Team XAL2005A
outcome: 1 fatality; 1 critical (second degree burns ~28% of body plus inhalation injury); 2 minor burn/inhalation injuries; no fire shelter deployed (spare shelters in cab considered); engine driven out after the front passed
key_timing: Fire reported 17:37 Oct 25. Oct 29: by 11:00 fire crossed Hwy 78; ~12:00 to 12:15 E6162 assigned to 920 Orchard Ln; ~12:25 firing at 930 Orchard; ~12:35 Strike Team Leader visits, leaves; ~5 min later crew sees increased activity below; Novato report: ~12:45 increases in intensity, ~13:00 rapid increase. Run covered ~0.46 mi (about one-half mile) upslope in a little under 2 minutes. A photo taken ~20 s before conditions changed dramatically. Refuge (house rear door) about 170 ft from the engine.
weather_at_event: Onshore gradient, sustained 17 mph with gust 31 mph from W; at 14:30 at site 70 F, RH 30%; Palmer Drought Index -2.88; live fuel moisture below critical
fire_behavior: Running crown fire in Fuel Model 4 brush (at least 90% crown closure) and FM1 grass; flame lengths over 78 ft, fireline intensity over 73,989 BTU/ft/s, ROS over 16 mph at 31 mph wind; site at top of a chimney, slopes 12 to 20%, elevation 3,800 ft, 400 ft above drainage bottom
escape_route_safety_zone_notes: Crew judged site defendable using a cleared area; house and engine designated refuge; access was a 10 ft wide, 490 ft long brush-overgrown driveway. No dedicated lookout could see the drainage; only the Captain had a portable radio. Green Sheet notes a refuge area differs from a safety zone and travel must be judged under worst case.
relevance_to_UQ: Gives a clean fire-arrival time scale (0.46 mi in under 2 min, about 20 s warning) against a 170 ft egress, i.e. a case where T_detect plus T_egress exceeded available time, anchoring the negative tail of the margin.

event_name: A Classification of US Wildland Firefighter Entrapments Based on Coincident Fuels, Weather, and Topography (Page, Freeborn, Butler, Jolly), Fire 2(4):52, DOI 10.3390/fire2040052
people_involved: 166 entrapments, 1202 people, 117 fatalities, 1981 to 2017, conterminous US
outcome: Four archetypes: low fire danger; high danger plus steep slope; high danger plus low canopy; high danger plus high canopy. Entrapments occur across wide conditions including low danger and flat terrain.
relevance_to_UQ: Gives conditional entrapment frequencies by environment class, usable as stratified priors.
